summary: Mobile responsiveness sweep across iPhone (390x844), iPad (768x1024) and Desktop (1440x900). 6 of 7 test scenarios PASS. One functional deviation found: mobile buyer-form inputs render at 15.2px (0.95rem) instead of the required >=16px, meaning iOS Safari WILL trigger auto-zoom on focus — contradicting the claim in the feature list. All other requirements verified: hamburger drawer, 7 nav testids, drawer opens/closes correctly, no horizontal scroll on 390, doogie-fab visible at 60x60, cookie-banner stacked above FAB, compliance strip full lead-in hidden on mobile, tablet grid-3 single-column, desktop nav restored, all 10 regression routes return 200.

ui_bugs.component: BuyerIntake form (.field input/select/textarea) — and by extension every form using the .field wrapper (seller, admin, valuation, etc.)
ui_bugs.issue: Computed font-size on mobile is 15.2px (0.95rem) on buyer-name, buyer-email, buyer-phone, buyer-type, buyer-under-contract, buyer-casl, buyer-pipa, and all <select>/<textarea>. iOS Safari triggers input auto-zoom whenever a focused form control is <16px. The global rule at /app/frontend/src/index.css:156 `input, textarea, select, button { font-size: 16px; }` is being overridden by the more specific rule at line 116 `.field input, .field select, .field textarea { ... font-size: 0.95rem; }`. Requirement #3 in the review request (verify computed font-size >=16px on any input) FAILS.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/index.css, either bump `.field input, .field select, .field textarea` (line 116) to `font-size: 16px;` OR add an override in the mobile-first block, e.g.: `@media(max-width: 700px) { .field input, .field select, .field textarea { font-size: 16px; } }`. Same rule should apply to the search-bar input (line 190 currently sets 0.95rem on mobile → 15.2px, will also auto-zoom on iOS).
critical_code_review_comments: The global mobile-zoom-prevention rule `input, textarea, select, button { font-size: 16px; }` is defeated by every more-specific existing rule (.field input, .search-bar input, .doogie-panel form input). Either use `!important` on the global mobile rule inside a `@media(max-width: 700px)` block, or bump the base font-size on those specific selectors to 16px at mobile breakpoint. Currently the claimed iOS-auto-zoom prevention is only partially working.
App.js is still ~1482 lines (previously flagged in iteration_5). Splitting into pages/, components/, forms/, legal/ modules would improve maintainability. Not a functional issue.

BCFSA licence number is still literal '[Doug to add]' placeholder (data-testid=licence-num). Must be filled in before production launch to actually satisfy BCFSA advertising rules (already flagged in iteration_5).

rca_of_the_issue.bug: iOS Safari auto-zoom NOT actually prevented on .field-wrapped form inputs and .search-bar input
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: 1) Open https://proptech-hub-111.preview.emergentagent.com/buyer at viewport 390x844. 2) Evaluate `parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-testid="buyer-name"]')).fontSize)` in the console. 3) Result is 15.2 (expected >=16).
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: CSS specificity — the global rule `input, textarea, select, button { font-size: 16px; }` at /app/frontend/src/index.css:156 has selector-specificity (0,0,1) while `.field input, .field select, .field textarea { font-size: 0.95rem; }` at line 116 has specificity (0,1,1) and therefore wins. Same problem for `.search-bar input { font-size: 1rem; }` desktop and `.search-bar input { font-size: 0.95rem; }` mobile (line 190).
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Option A (recommended): inside the existing `@media(max-width: 700px)` block, add `.field input, .field select, .field textarea, .search-bar input { font-size: 16px; }`. Option B: change `.field input, .field select, .field textarea` base rule to `font-size: 1rem` (16px). Option A is preferred — it only touches mobile and preserves desktop density.
